question: What is the System Demo in SAFe?
options: A demo of the results of one team at the end of its sprint
A demo of the draft plan during the PI Planning event
A review of the integrated product at the end of the PI
A sales demo of the product for potential new customers
explanation: The PI System Demo is shown in week 10 to the entire ART and stakeholders.

question: How long is the PI Planning event?
explanation: A two-day event for all teams.

question: PI Planning is attended only by the Release Train Engineer and Product Management.
explanation: It is an event for all teams of the ART; only the evening management review is leadership-only.

question: How does PI Planning Day 1 start?
options: With team breakouts to identify stories and risks
With the business context and the visions for the ART
With the confidence vote on the final plans of all the teams
With the inspect & adapt workshop of the last PI
explanation: Day 1 morning: business context, product/solution vision and architecture vision (entire ART). Afternoon: planning context, team breakouts #1 (identify stories, estimate story points, identify risks), draft plan review.

question: Who attends the "Management Review & Problem Solving" on the evening of PI Planning Day 1?
options: The entire ART including all team members
The Scrum Masters of all the teams
The Product Owners of all the teams
explanation: It is the only leadership-only session: RTE, Product Management, Business Owners and Architects.

question: What do teams do in Team Breakouts #1 of PI Planning Day 1?
options: Vote on their confidence in the final plan
Hold a retrospective on the previous PI
Identify stories, estimate and identify risks
explanation: Teams identify stories, estimate story points and identify risks. Breakouts #2 on Day 2 finalize plans and align dependencies.

question: Which activity is part of PI Planning Day 2?
options: The final plan review with a confidence vote
The business context presentation by the owners
The PI System Demo with all the stakeholders
The Scrum of Scrums with the Scrum Masters
explanation: Day 2: team breakouts #2, final plan review and confidence vote, PI objectives presented and approved, program board finalized, PI planning retrospective led by the RTE.

question: Who leads the PI Planning Retrospective?
options: The System Architect of the ART
The Product Manager of the ART
explanation: It is the last activity of Day 2.

question: Which SAFe role coordinates the ART and facilitates the ART meetings, comparable to a team's Scrum Master?
explanation: Some material writes "TRE", but the role is the RTE.
flag: The slide abbreviates it "TRE" in one place; it means the Release Train Engineer (RTE).

question: Which SAFe role ensures technical integrity and defines the architectural guidelines for the teams?
explanation: Other roles: Product Owner (program level) and Scrum of Scrums Master (facilitator of the team Scrum Master meetings).

question: In which week of the PI table does Inspect & Adapt take place?
explanation: Week 0 prep, week 1 PI Planning (2 days), weeks 1-10 execution (5 sprints), week 10 I&A (1 day), week 11+ next PI Planning.

question: What happens in the problem-solving workshop of Inspect & Adapt?
options: The system demo of the work of all teams
Root cause analysis and action items in breakouts
The vote on the PI objectives that are presented to the ART
The planning of the next sprint of each team
explanation: I&A: PI System Demo (1-2 hrs), quantitative and qualitative measurement (1 hr), problem-solving workshop with root cause analysis and action items, done by the entire ART in breakouts (1 hr), confidence vote on improvement actions (15 min).

question: Which ART-level meeting combines the Scrum of Scrums and the PO Sync?
explanation: SoS (SMs, RTE), PO Sync (POs, Product Management, Business Owners) and ART Sync are weekly; the System Demo is at the end of the PI.

question: Who attends the Sprint Retrospective of a team during the PI cycle?
options: The team, the PO and stakeholders
Only the Scrum Masters of all teams
The team and the Scrum Master
explanation: Sprint Review: team, PO and stakeholders at the end of the sprint.

question: Who attends the Sprint Review of a team during the PI cycle?
options: The team, the Product Owner and stakeholders
The team and the Scrum Master
The Product Owner and the Scrum Master
The entire ART together with the company's CEO
explanation: Sprint Retrospective: team and Scrum Master.

question: How often does the Scrum of Scrums take place in the SAFe ART?
explanation: Attendees: Scrum Masters, RTE and others with dependencies.

question: Which S@S group resolves escalated impediments and takes strategic decisions?
explanation: EAT: CPO, SoSM, CEO and company managers; facilitates team clusters in the double-scaled setting.

question: Who coordinates the Product Owner team in S@S?
explanation: The SoSM facilitates the teams.

question: Who facilitates the teams in S@S?
explanation: SoSM: facilitate teams. CPO: coordinates the PO team.

question: Who attends the Scaled Daily Scrum?
options: The Product Owners of all the teams
One representative per team and the SoSM
All members of all the teams together
The Executive Action Team and the CEO
explanation: At least one representative per team, plus the Scrum of Scrums Master. Daily, 15 minutes; focus on cross-team progress and impediments.

question: Who attends the Scaled Retrospective?
options: The Scrum Masters of each team
explanation: All Scrum Masters of each team take part.

question: What is the purpose of the Executive MetaScrum (EMS)?
options: To coordinate daily progress between teams
To plan the next sprint of each team
To run the retrospective for all of the teams
To prioritize the shared backlog and align goals
explanation: The CPO and the POs meet in the Executive MetaScrum to prioritize the shared backlog and align goals. In S@S there is one backlog for all teams.
flag: Slide 19 says the EMS meets "at least once per sprint"; the events table (slide 24) lists the MetaScrum as weekly (1 hr).

question: How many backlogs do the teams share in S@S?
options: One for each Scrum of Scrums
One backlog for each Product Owner
explanation: The MetaScrum prioritizes it.

question: In S@S each team prioritizes its own separate backlog and the Chief Product Owner has no backlog.
explanation: The CPO and POs prioritize one backlog for all teams (the recap names a "CPO backlog").

question: What takes place in week 10 of the S@S cycle?
options: Scrum of Scrums planning of the next cycle
Inspect & Adapt with the scaled retrospective
The start of the first sprint of the cycle
explanation: Week 10 is Inspect & Adapt: scaled retrospective and Executive Action Team review. Week 0 is preparation (EMS), week 1 planning and alignment, weeks 1-10 execution (5 sprints), week 11+ next cycle planning.

question: How can the first comparison between SAFe and Scrum@Scale be summarized?
options: SAFe is minimalistic, S@S is elaborate
S@S is only for software, SAFe for hardware
SAFe is elaborate, S@S is minimalistic
explanation: "Both frameworks have a completely different approach."

question: In Scrum@Scale, what is a group of five Scrum of Scrums that together cover 25 teams called?
options: A SoSoS (Scrum of Scrum of Scrums)
An Executive Action Team that covers 25 teams
explanation: The scaling drawings show a Scrum team (SM + PO), a SoS of 5 teams and a "SoSoS of 25 Teams".
flag: Image slide: read from the slide picture.

question: How often does the Scrum of Scrums meet in S@S?
explanation: Attendees: Scrum Masters, team reps and the SoSM; resolves delivery impediments.

question: A PI Planning event lasts ____ days.
explanation: PI Planning is a two-day event for all teams.

question: It is advised to reward an SPO for attrition rates below ____ percent.
explanation: Attrition targets: below 10%.

question: SPO is short for service ____ organisation (the IT provider).
explanation: SRO = service receiving organisation.

question: ITIL has 3 process clusters and ____ processes.
explanation: ITIL: 3 process clusters, 34 processes.

question: A disruptive technology is typically lower priced or designed for a different set of ____ or market place.
explanation: From the definition of a disruptive technology.

question: An organisational structure that is efficient in one situation stays efficient after a take-over or merger.
explanation: Structure must be aligned with the changing strategy and redesigned in any new situation.

question: Top IT SPOs are described as replicating their own behaviour to their customers.
explanation: They push their customers to greater achievements too.

question: Exit management should only be thought about when the contract ends.
explanation: Prepare the exit at the start of the relationship.

question: Existing companies can defend against disruptive entrants by modernizing their old services, for example chain stores starting webshops.
explanation: These are called sustaining innovations.

question: The audit procedure consists of eight steps.
explanation: Plan, kickoff, gather data and test, interview, review observations, analyze and report, respond to findings, issue final report.

question: Explain vendor lock-in and name three measures to prevent it.
modelAnswer: Vendor lock-in is too much dependency on the SPO, so you cannot get rid of it. Measures: perform at least 20% of IT services in-house; let IT staff spread across all IT functions of the SPO to learn the outsourced work; fill key positions in outsourced projects (architecture, lead designers, lead developers).
flag: Lecture 5 adds knowledge-management measures (e.g. a minimum of 25% SRO personnel).

question: List the elements of exit management.
modelAnswer: Scope and duration; governance during the exit (treated as a project); deliverables and documentation; employee transfer clause; knowledge transition (e.g. shadowing); intellectual property; financial terms; cooperation of the incumbent SPO; exit plan testing (e.g. once every 2 years on non-core business days).
explanation: Prepare the exit at the start of the relationship.

question: Describe the eight steps of the IT audit procedure and say who is responsible for each.
modelAnswer: 1 Plan the audit (auditor). 2 Hold the kickoff meeting (auditor/organization). 3 Gather data and test IT controls (auditor/organization). 4 Interview responsible managers and employees (auditor/organization). 5 Review observations (auditor/organization). 6 Analyze and report findings (auditor). 7 Respond to findings (organization). 8 Issue the final report (auditor).

question: What makes a recommendation in an audit report useful?
modelAnswer: It explains how to achieve something (not only what to do), is tied directly to a finding, is actionable within organisational constraints, has measurable outcomes, names who is responsible, has a clear and reasonable deadline, and includes a relevant working example as proof.

question: Compare SAFe and Scrum@Scale in a few sentences.
modelAnswer: A first comparison: SAFe is elaborate, Scrum@Scale is minimalistic. SAFe uses an Agile Release Train of teams, a PI cycle of 4-5 sprints, a 2-day PI Planning event and roles such as the RTE and System Architect. S@S scales with a Scrum of Scrums (SoSM), a Chief Product Owner with one shared backlog, an Executive MetaScrum, Executive Action Team and scaled events such as the Scaled Daily Scrum.
flag: The slides give only a first comparison; for deeper pros and cons use your debate preparation.

question: List the reasons for outsourcing.
modelAnswer: Save money; focus on the core business; higher investments in the business instead of IT; reduce risk (of getting behind in IT); quick access to IT talent (by hiring an innovative SPO).

question: The Apple iPhone that outperformed all its competitors was sold initially at a very high price. This is an example of:
explanation: Top-down: new products that outperform the existing ones, sold at a higher price at first (Apple, Tesla, PlayStation, Samsung). Low-end disruption is cheap and simple, and new-market disruption takes an innovation to a new market. "Product focused" is not one of the three market approaches.

question: What is true for IT Management Frameworks?
options: Process Maturity is part of every IT Management audit
They consist of a hierarchy of process clusters, processes and practices
COBIT derives from (technical quality and) standardisation organisations
The existing IT management frameworks differ significantly from each other
explanation: Frameworks are a structured set of processes, practices and professional products. ITIL has 3 process clusters with 34 processes, and COBIT has 5 domains, 37 processes and 210 practices. The other statements are not part of the course material.

question: What is the frequency of the scaled variant of the Daily Scrum (the Scrum of Scrums) in the SAFe framework?
explanation: In SAFe the Scrum of Scrums is a weekly ART-level meeting. Do not mix it up with Scrum at Scale, where the Scaled Daily Scrum takes place every day for 15 minutes.

question: What is a good way to prevent a vendor lock-in?
options: keep a part of the IT personnel inhouse
go for long contracts, at least 5 years
agree on a high percentage of experienced SPO employees in the contract
agree on penalties in the contract if an SPO underperforms
explanation: Vendor lock-in is too much dependency on the SPO. Perform at least 20% of the IT services in-house, let your IT staff spread across the SPO's functions, and fill key positions in outsourced projects. Contract length, the staff pyramid and penalties do not reduce the dependency.

question: What is the duration of a PI cycle in the SAFe framework?
explanation: A PI cycle is 4 or 5 two-week sprints, so 8 to 12 weeks. Two weeks is one sprint. The PI table shows the 5-sprint version of about 10 weeks.

question: Which answer is NOT a part of the Sarbanes Oxley Act?
options: Disclosure of knowable conflicts of interests
explanation: SOX lists: the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, auditor independence, corporate responsibility, internal control (a yearly quality rating), enhanced financial disclosure, disclosure of knowable conflicts of interests and penalties for misconduct. Monthly integrity audits are not in it.

question: Which of the following 'selling points' of SPO's is NOT advisable for an SRO?
explanation: Always choose innovation over price: organisations traditionally look at the lowest price, but the value comes from an SPO that helps to reduce cost, manage complexity and adopt innovations. Technical, client-facing and business expertise are differentiators to look for.

question: How is the backlog structured in the S@S framework?
options: The SoS backlog contains epics, the team backlogs contain userstories
There is one backlog for all teams
There is no overarching backlog for the teams, each teams has its own backlog
There is no backlog in the S@S framework
explanation: The Executive MetaScrum (the Chief Product Owner and the POs) prioritizes one backlog for all teams. The recap names a "CPO backlog".

question: An SPO has 8 experienced people, 9 medium experienced people and 10 employees with few experience working for your SRO.
options: this is a heavy pyramid, ideal for tough jobs
this is a heavy pyramid, ideal for light jobs
this is a lean pyramid, ideal for tough jobs
this is a lean pyramid, ideal for light jobs
explanation: A heavy pyramid has a lot of experienced people and suits tough jobs. A lean pyramid has few experienced people and many freshers (0 to 3 years) and suits light jobs. Here the three levels are close to equal, so a good part of the staff is experienced: a heavy pyramid.
flag: The slides do not say where a pyramid stops being lean and becomes heavy. The answer is the one marked in the professor's practice test.

question: What is true for a 'good' SPO for the SRO?
explanation: All levels (hierarchy) must be covered by both organisations, so the SRO and the SPO have counterparts at every level. A good SPO uses consultative selling and has a low (not high) attrition rate. "Strong general services" is not a criterion.

question: What is a good way to manage your SPO?
options: always approach the SPO personnel via their service managers
Go for the highest service and production levels
treat the SPO personnel as your own colleagues
Show confidence in your SPO, so don't constantly check their performance
explanation: DO: treat the SPO personnel as your own colleagues, and get to know the SPO's key people (especially the horizontals), not only the service managers. Monitor the SPO so that its weaknesses do not become apparent, and make realistic agreements instead of promising the highest levels.

question: In which two main categories could IT play a role in disruptive innovations?
options: IT as an innovative product and IT supporting innovative processes
IT supporting innovative processes and IT supporting action plans
IT as an innovative product and IT supporting an innovation
IT supporting innovative processes and IT supporting new business models
explanation: The basic question of strategic IT decisions: is IT the business product (strategy A), or does IT support the business (strategy B)?
flag: The slides name two roles for IT: the business product and a support to the business. The wording of the right option comes from the professor's practice test.

question: Why is SOX legislation important for IT Management?
options: IT facilitates the instruments for governance audits
IT is conditional for administrative transparency in organisations
The positions of IT managers are prone to abuse
IT infrastructure accounts for a key part of the total cost structure
explanation: SOX is about control and transparency of what a public organisation reports. That administration runs on IT, so IT has to be in control as well: the "SOX for IT" list (IT general controls) covers change management, access policies, incident management and so on.
flag: The slides do not say in one sentence why SOX matters for IT. The answer is the one marked in the professor's practice test; the explanation links it to the IT general controls on slide 8.

question: What is true for a comparison between SAFe and S@S?
options: SAFe is expandable in 3 levels, S@S is not expandable
SAFe has incorporated a lot of management methods like LEAN, DEVOPS and management of change, S@S has not
SAFe is more agile than S@S because it has a scheduled PI cycle
S@S is more agile than SAFe because it added roles like the RTE and the System Architect
explanation: SAFe is the elaborate framework: its essential configuration includes Lean-Agile leadership, built-in quality, continuous delivery and DevOps. S@S is the minimalistic one. The RTE and the System Architect are SAFe roles, not S@S roles, and S@S has a cycle too.

question: Should you go for an overseas IT department?
options: Yes, but only if you are able to focus on your core business; this advantage is often underestimated besides the financial benefits and motivational and cultural issues
No, overseas personnel is significantly less motivated and cultural communication issues outweigh financial benefits
Yes, low cost is key; the benefits generally outweigh disadvantages like low employee motivation and cultural distance
Yes, but only if you invest in face to face interactions to manage motivational and cultural issues
explanation: Yes, with a condition. An own overseas department (a captive) is often seen as a cost centre, which gives low empowerment and low motivation, and cultural differences add to it. Face-to-face interactions are essential: letting employees and management travel across is worth the money.

question: A company develops the idea of self-steering buses. A prototype is very promising. Which part of the BCG matrix does this situation correspond to?
explanation: A question mark has high market growth but a low market share: promising, but not yet proven. A star has high growth and high share, a cow low growth and high share, and a dog low growth and low share.

question: What contractual agreement is NOT part of 'Exit Management'?
options: who pays for the exit project
availability and performance levels during the exit phase
(forced) cooperation of the incumbent SPO during exit phase
explanation: Exit management covers: scope and duration, governance (a project), deliverables, the employee transfer clause, knowledge transition, intellectual property, financial terms (who pays), cooperation of the incumbent SPO, and exit plan testing. Availability and performance levels are not on that list.

question: What is the best definition of 'horizontals' in an organisation in the context of Outsourcing?
explanation: Horizontals are the general technical services (infrastructure, testing, BI) that serve all customers across the verticals. The verticals are the industry-specific services, and the supporting services are the general supporting departments.

question: What is true?
options: ITIL consists of more than 100 processes
IT Management frameworks derive from quality management, financial management and human resource management
Audits are meant to check if processes are compliant with reference models
the process maturity model was invented by COBIT
explanation: An audit checks reality against standards and reference models (compliance, conformity). ITIL has 34 processes in 3 clusters, and the maturity levels come from CMMI, not COBIT. The origin of the frameworks is not part of the course material.

question: What is true?
options: S@S is not suited for bigger organisations
The S@S planning event takes one day
The SAFe Inspect & Adapt event takes two days
SAFe is not suitable for organizations with fewer than 10 teams
explanation: The S@S Preparation & Planning day: the Executive MetaScrum in the morning and the Scrum of Scrums planning in the afternoon. S@S has scaling options for bigger organisations, SAFe's Inspect & Adapt takes 1 day, and an ART has 5 to 12 teams.

question: In general, what do IT management frameworks consist of?
options: A list of laws that every organisation must obey in its IT department
One single process that every IT department has to copy without changes
A structured set of processes, practices and professional products
The audit reports of all the organisations that use the framework
explanation: Frameworks like ITIL, COBIT and ISO consist of a structured set of processes, practices and professional products.

question: What is an IT audit meant to check?
options: Whether reality complies with the standards and reference models
Whether the organisation uses the newest version of its framework
Whether the IT department is the largest one in its whole sector
Whether the IT provider offers the lowest price on the market
explanation: Reference models and standards are checked against reality: compliance, conformity, accordance, consent.

question: ITIL consists of more than 100 processes.
explanation: ITIL has 3 process clusters and 34 processes. COBIT has 37 processes and ISO 20000 has 30.

question: How often is the internal control of a public organisation rated under SOX?
explanation: SOX lists "internal control (yearly quality rating)". There are no monthly audits in the list.

question: Nobody in a company can tell who changed the software in production, or when. Which IT general control (ITGC) is weak?
options: Physical security of the data centre
explanation: Change management, including software change and configuration management (version control), keeps track of who changes what and when.

question: A new airline sells simple, cheap flights without extras and takes customers from the established airlines. It uses no new technology. Which type of disruption is this?
explanation: Low-end disruption: established companies add features at a too high pace, so simple cheap products win at the low end (Aldi, Ryanair, IKEA). It does not need new technology.

question: An app on the mobile internet brings an existing service to a group of customers who did not use it before. Which type of disruption is this?
explanation: New-market disruption extends an innovation to a new market (eBay, Uber, the e-bike). It uses new technology, often internet or mobile technology in existing markets.

question: In the BCG matrix, which product has a low market growth but a high market share?
explanation: A cow has low growth and high share: it brings in money. A star has high growth and high share (invest), a question mark high growth and low share (prioritize or divest), a dog low growth and low share (kill).

question: In the BCG matrix, what is the advice for a question mark?
options: Invest in it, then let it become a dog
Leave it alone: it is stable
explanation: The arrows from the question mark say "prioritize" (towards a star) and "divest". A dog is killed, and a star gets investment.

question: Which block of the Business Model Canvas shows what a company earns from its customers?
explanation: Revenue Streams sits next to Cost Structure at the bottom of the canvas. The other blocks: Key Partners, Key Activities, Key Resources, Value Propositions, Customer Relationships, Channels and Customer Segments.

question: An SPO's employees worked 1,200 billable hours out of 1,600 working hours. What is the utilization rate?
explanation: Utilization rate = billable hours ÷ working hours = 1,200 ÷ 1,600 = 75%.

question: An SPO loses a quarter of its employees every year. What does this high attrition rate suggest?
options: A very efficient service provider with satisfied customers
A fair employee appraisal system that rewards high performance
Superior business domain skills that keep staff loyal
Poorly motivated personnel and unstable service delivery
explanation: Low attrition rates indicate better motivated personnel. Employee stability (measured by the attrition rate) is a hygiene criterion because it shows the continuity of service delivery.

question: Which is a way for an SPO to distinguish itself in the market?
options: Offering exactly the same services as every other SPO in the market
Knowing and speaking the local market habits and language
Never changing its organisational structure after a take-over
Keeping its employees away from the customers it serves
explanation: SPOs distinguish themselves by best client facing managers, business expertise, local market habits and language, the cheapest qualified labour force, technical edge expertise and methodological expertise.

question: To prevent vendor lock-in, the SRO can fill key positions in outsourced projects, such as architecture, lead designers and lead developers.
explanation: Other measures: perform at least 20% of the IT services in-house, and let IT staff spread across all IT functions of the SPO.

question: Which of these would increase the risk of vendor lock-in?
options: Performing at least 20% of the IT services in-house at the SRO
Letting your own IT staff learn the work that is outsourced
Giving all key positions in the outsourced project to the SPO
Keeping SRO personnel on the key positions of the project
explanation: Lock-in is too much dependency on the SPO. Giving away all key positions (architecture, lead designers, lead developers) means the knowledge is only with the SPO.

question: For which kind of work is a lean pyramid suitable?
explanation: A lean pyramid has few experienced and many inexperienced people, which suits light jobs. Tough jobs need a heavy pyramid (more experience).

question: An SPO team has 2 people with more than 10 years of experience and 20 freshers with 0 to 3 years. How do you describe this team?
options: A lean pyramid, ideal for tough jobs
A heavy pyramid, ideal for light jobs
A heavy pyramid, ideal for tough jobs
A lean pyramid, ideal for light jobs
explanation: Very few experienced people and a lot of freshers: a lean pyramid, suited for light jobs.

question: In the contract, agreements should be made about the pyramid: the balance of experienced and inexperienced employees.
explanation: The contract should say how experienced and inexperienced staff are balanced.

question: Letting employees and management travel to your overseas IT department is worth the money.
explanation: Face-to-face interactions have appeared to be essential. Collaboration between both organisations leads to motivation; just taking orders from headquarters leads to demotivation.

question: The agreements for the exit phase should include the cooperation of the incumbent SPO.
explanation: During the exit phase many unforeseen situations occur, so agree beforehand that the incumbent SPO will cooperate.

question: Which minimum percentage of SRO personnel is given as an example for keeping knowledge inside?
explanation: Agree on a minimum percentage (for example 25%) of SRO personnel. Do not confuse it with the 20% of IT services performed in-house and the 10% attrition target.

question: How long does the Inspect & Adapt event at the end of the PI cycle take?
explanation: Inspect & Adapt takes 1 day in week 10. PI Planning takes 2 days.

question: SAFe's essential configuration includes Lean-Agile leadership and DevOps.
explanation: SAFe's essential configuration includes Lean-Agile leadership (mindset, core values, SAFe principles), built-in quality, continuous delivery and a DevOps component. That is why SAFe is called the elaborate framework.

question: How do the SAFe Scrum of Scrums and the S@S Scaled Daily Scrum differ in frequency?
options: The SAFe Scrum of Scrums is weekly; the S@S Scaled Daily Scrum is daily
The SAFe Scrum of Scrums is daily; the S@S Scaled Daily Scrum is weekly
explanation: SAFe: Scrum of Scrums weekly. S@S: Scaled Daily Scrum daily for 15 minutes, and a separate weekly Scrum of Scrums of 30 to 60 minutes.

question: Which role belongs to Scrum at Scale?
explanation: S@S roles: Scrum of Scrums Master, Chief Product Owner and the Executive Action Team. The RTE and the System Architect are SAFe roles.

question: How is the Preparation & Planning day of an S@S cycle organised?
options: Scrum of Scrums planning in the morning, Executive MetaScrum in the afternoon
Executive MetaScrum in the morning, Scrum of Scrums planning in the afternoon
Two days of PI Planning with all teams
A one-hour Scaled Daily Scrum only
explanation: Morning: Executive MetaScrum (review vision, prioritize the shared backlog). Afternoon: Scrum of Scrums planning (teams plan sprints, identify impediments). Backlog refinement goes on in between.

question: Explain the difference between a heavy and a lean pyramid and say when you use each.
modelAnswer: A pyramid is the balance of experienced and inexperienced staff (more than 10 years at the top, 0 to 3 years "freshers" at the bottom). A heavy pyramid has relatively more experienced people and is used for tough jobs. A lean pyramid has few experienced people and many freshers and is used for light jobs. The balance should be agreed in the contract.

question: Name the three market approaches of disruptive innovation and give an example of each.
modelAnswer: Low-end disruption: simple, cheap products because established companies add too many features (Aldi, Ryanair, IKEA), no new technology. New-market disruption: an innovation taken to a new market, often with internet or mobile technology (eBay, Uber, e-bike). Top-down: new products that outperform the existing ones, sold at a higher price first (Apple, Tesla, PlayStation, Samsung).

question: Which of these is a responsibility of public organisations under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX)?
options: Mandatory use of the COBIT framework for all IT processes
A monthly integrity audit of every department by the board
Free choice of the external auditor by the CEO of the company
explanation: SOX lists the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, auditor independence, corporate responsibility, internal control, enhanced financial disclosure, disclosure of knowable conflicts of interests and penalties for misconduct.

question: Which SOX responsibility is about items that are not on the balance sheet?
options: Internal control (yearly quality rating) of the whole organisation
Disclosure of knowable conflicts of interests
explanation: Enhanced financial disclosure covers off-balance-sheet items.

question: Which SOX responsibility makes individual managers answerable for what their organisation reports?
options: Disclosure of knowable conflicts of interests of the managers
Disclosure of knowable conflicts of interests
explanation: Corporate responsibility is the individual responsibility of managers.

question: Which statement about the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) is true?
options: It requires every public company to use ITIL for its IT department
Penalties for misconduct are one of its responsibilities
It only applies to the IT department of a public company
It was written for European companies only, with code Tabaksblat
explanation: Penalties for misconduct are on the SOX list. The European code Tabaksblat and IFRS are named as European affiliates, so SOX itself is not a European law.

question: Which of these is NOT an IT general control (ITGC) under "SOX for IT"?
options: Access policies for the IT systems
Disaster recovery of systems and data
Physical security of the IT infrastructure
explanation: The ITGC list: change management, version control, software development standards, access policies, incident management, problem management, technical support policies, implementation and testing procedures, disaster recovery and physical security.

question: Anyone who walks in can enter the server room of a company. Which IT general control is weak?
explanation: Physical security is one of the ITGC items under SOX for IT.

question: After a flood a company cannot restore its systems and data. Which IT general control is missing?
explanation: Disaster recovery is an ITGC item.

question: Which IT general control makes sure new software is checked before it goes live?
options: Access policies for the users of the IT systems
explanation: Implementation and testing procedures are an ITGC item.

question: Which IT general control keeps track of the versions of the software?
options: Incident management of failures in the daily operation
explanation: Change management includes software change and configuration management (version control).

question: Which regulation is named in the IT audit principles for obeying laws and for ethics?
explanation: The audit principles name "Obey laws (SOX, VAR)" and "Ethics (SOX)".

question: Which European code is named as an affiliate of SOX?
explanation: European affiliates of SOX: code Tabaksblat and IFRS.

question: Which is the full name of the act that SOX stands for?
options: Public Company IT Governance and Audit Control Act
Public Company Accounting Reform and Investor Protection Act
Financial Reporting and Software Control Standards Act
International Corporate Ethics, Disclosure and Software Regulation Act
explanation: SOX is the Public Company Accounting Reform and Investor Protection Act, named after Sarbanes and Oxley.

question: A manager signs off figures he knows are wrong. Which SOX element applies most directly?
options: The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board
explanation: SOX includes penalties for misconduct.

question: Which pairing of subject and framework is NOT correct?
explanation: IT security belongs to ISO 27001. PRINCE2 is the framework for IT projects.

question: Which pairing of subject and framework is correct?
explanation: Running software: DevOps. IT projects: PRINCE2. Process improvement: LEAN. IT architecture: TOGAF.

question: Which statement about COBIT is true?
options: It has 3 process clusters and 34 processes
It has 5 maturity levels and 24 process areas
explanation: COBIT: 2 areas, 5 domains, 37 processes, 210 practices and 1112 activities. The other numbers belong to ITIL, CMMI and ISO 27001.

question: Which statement about CMMI is true?
options: It has 5 domains and 37 processes, with 210 practices
It has 3 process clusters and 34 processes
It has 5 maturity levels and 24 process areas
explanation: CMMI introduces maturity levels: 5 levels and 24 process areas.

question: Which description fits ISO 27001?
options: IT service management with 30 processes, like ITIL
Quality management for every kind of organisation
Maturity levels for rating and improving processes
explanation: ISO 27001 is information security management with 114 controls (policies).

question: Which description fits ISO 20000 (BS 15000)?
options: Maturity levels developed at Carnegie Mellon University
Enterprise architecture with a method for the architects
IT service management with 30 processes, like ITIL
explanation: ISO 20000 (BS 15000) is IT service management with 30 processes, like ITIL.

question: Which of these is a "profitability" goal of an IT governance framework?
explanation: Ensure ROI, assure business value and satisfy stakeholder needs are the profitability goals. The others are control goals.

question: Which of these is a "control" goal of an IT governance framework?
explanation: Measurable results, key metrics, procedures to control, rights and responsibilities, and mitigating risks are control goals.

question: Which framework answers the question "How do I keep control over my finance?"
options: ITIL (best practice for IT service management)
explanation: COBIT and COSO are rules and procedures. ITIL, BiSL, ASL, ISM and MOF are best practices. ISO, ANSI and BSI are standards.

question: Which of these is a standard that answers "How do I control my quality?"
explanation: The standards that answer how to control quality are ISO, ANSI and BSI.

question: In the survey of IT management framework adoption (Informa Tech, January 2022), which framework was followed by 21%?
explanation: In the chart: ITIL v4 and hybrid 40% each, ITIL v3 26%, COBIT 21%, TOGAF 10%, eTOM 5%.

question: An auditor compares what a team really does with the standards it should follow. What is this check about?
options: The maturity of the budget of the IT department
explanation: Standards and reference models are checked against reality: compliance, conformity, accordance, consent.

question: Which audit step is done by the auditor and the organization together?
explanation: Review observations is step 5, done by the auditor and the organization. Analysis and the final report are the auditor's, responding is the organization's.

question: Which audit step is carried out by the organization alone?
explanation: Respond to findings (step 7) is the organization's.

question: Which audit step comes directly after "Review observations"?
options: Gather data and test IT controls
explanation: Steps 5 to 8: review observations, analyze and report findings, respond to findings, issue final report.

question: Which audit step comes directly before "Issue final report"?
explanation: The organization responds to the findings (step 7) before the auditor issues the final report (step 8).

question: After the audit the organization makes a plan to fix the shortcomings the auditor reported. Which part of the audit is this?
options: The audit kickoff meeting with the organization
explanation: Follow-up: identified shortcomings (reported by the auditor), improvement plan (organization), execute the measures, optional internal audits, prepare for the next audit.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the IT audit principles?
options: Say what you do, do what you say, prove it
Hide weaknesses until the final report
explanation: The principles: being in control, say what you do, do what you say, prove it, professionalism and best practices, reference to standards, obey laws, ethics.

question: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of a useful recommendation?
options: It names an owner who is responsible for the action
It is general, so it fits every organisation
It has a clear and reasonable deadline
It is tied directly to a finding or problem
explanation: A useful recommendation is tied to a finding, actionable, measurable, has an owner and a deadline and a working example.

question: In the suggested report structure, which section comes directly after the Audit Findings?
explanation: Structure: title page, table of contents, executive summary, introduction, audit findings, recommendations, follow-up plan, conclusion, appendices.

question: Where do the appendices go in the suggested report structure?
options: Between the introduction and the findings
explanation: Appendices are number 9 of 9.

question: How should the executive summary of an audit report start?
options: With the history of the audit firm and its people
With a list of all the audit steps that were taken
With the appendices and the raw interview notes
With the most critical findings, quantified
explanation: Lead with the most critical findings, for example a prioritized table of high-risk issues, and quantify the impact.

question: Which of these makes a finding in an audit report credible?
options: A strongly worded opinion of the auditor about the manager
Verifiable evidence, such as data excerpts or benchmarks
A long description of the auditor's experience
A list of the names of everyone who was interviewed
explanation: Support every finding with verifiable evidence: charts, data excerpts or benchmarks.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the three market approaches of disruptive innovation?
options: A new market approach, with new technology
explanation: The three market approaches: low-end, new-market and top-down.

question: A furniture chain sells simple, cheap furniture and wins customers from the established brands. It uses no new technology. Which market approach is this?
explanation: Low-end disruption: simple, cheap products, no new technology (Aldi, Ryanair, IKEA).

question: A car maker launches an electric car that outperforms the existing cars. At first it is sold at a high price. Which market approach is this?
explanation: Top-down: new products that outperform the existing ones, sold at a higher price at first (Apple, Tesla, PlayStation, Samsung).

question: An online marketplace brings buying and selling to people who never used classified ads. It uses internet technology. Which market approach is this?
explanation: New-market disruption extends an innovation to a new market, with new technology (eBay, Uber, e-bike).

question: Which of these is given as an example of low-end disruption?
explanation: Low-end examples: Aldi, Ryanair, IKEA.

question: Which of these is given as an example of top-down disruption?
explanation: Top-down examples: Apple, Tesla, PlayStation, Samsung.

question: Which of these is given as an example of new-market disruption?
explanation: New-market examples: eBay, Uber, the e-bike.

question: Which of these is an example of innovation in the process (supporting) aspect?
options: The Apple iPhone as a product with superior performance
The Tesla car as a product
Coffee pads for a coffee machine
explanation: Process innovation: the Toyota production process (LEAN), Dell, Alibaba. Product innovation: Apple, Tesla.

question: Which of these is an example of "new combinations of existing elements"?
explanation: New combinations of existing elements: coffee pads, e-bikes, agricultural drones, smart watches, hybrid cars.

question: Which of these is NOT given as an example of disruption through new business models?
explanation: New business models: Dell, Amazon, Netflix, Spotify, Airbnb. Tesla is an example of superior performance.

question: A chain of bookshops starts selling online to keep its customers. What is this called?
explanation: Existing companies defend themselves by modernizing their old services or products: sustaining innovations. Example: chain stores start webshops.

question: Which strategy applies to a company whose primary business is IT?
options: Strategy B: optimise the IT support
Strategy A: IT as the primary product
A sustaining strategy only, without innovation
No IT strategy is needed at all
explanation: The basic question: is IT our primary business (A) or supportive to the business (B)?

question: Which of these steps belongs to "IT strategy B: Optimize IT support"?
options: Kill the dogs of the BCG matrix
Fill in all nine blocks of the Business Model Canvas first
Check what competitors do in the field of IT innovations
Choose the provider with the lowest price
explanation: Strategy B includes checking what competitors do with IT innovations, the abilities of the current IT platform and opportunities for reengineering.

question: A product has a high market growth and a high market share. In the BCG matrix it is...
explanation: Star: high growth, high share. Cow: low growth, high share. Question mark: high growth, low share. Dog: low growth, low share.

question: In the BCG matrix picture, what is the advice for a star?
explanation: The picture shows invest for a star, prioritize or divest for a question mark, and kill for a dog.

question: Which block of the Business Model Canvas describes the groups of people a company serves?
explanation: The nine blocks include Customer Segments, Customer Relationships and Channels.

question: Which block of the Business Model Canvas describes the benefit a company offers?
explanation: Value Propositions is the block in the middle of the canvas.

question: Which block of the Business Model Canvas describes how a company reaches its customers?
explanation: Channels is one of the nine blocks.

question: Which of these is NOT a block of the Business Model Canvas?
explanation: The blocks: Key Partners, Key Activities, Key Resources, Value Propositions, Customer Relationships, Channels, Customer Segments, Cost Structure, Revenue Streams.

question: Which of these is named as disruptive software of the near past?
explanation: Disruptive software of the near past: ChatGPT, Facebook, WhatsApp, Photoshop, Amazon Cloud services.

question: Which of these is NOT a reason for outsourcing?
options: Focus on the core business of the organisation
Keep all IT knowledge inside the company
explanation: Reasons: save money, focus on core business, higher investments in business, reduce risk, quick access to IT talent.

question: Which reason for outsourcing is about getting expertise quickly?
options: Save money on the IT budget
Higher investments in the business instead of IT
explanation: Quick access to IT talent is reached by hiring an innovative SPO.

question: Which of these is the "bottom line" of a service provider?
explanation: Revenue is the top line, profit margin the bottom line.

question: The staff of an SPO worked 140 billable hours out of 160 working hours. What is the utilization rate?
explanation: Utilization rate = billable hours ÷ working hours = 140 ÷ 160 = 87.5%.

question: Which party is the SRO?
options: The IT provider that delivers the services
The external auditor of the provider
explanation: SRO = service receiving organisation: the customer, the users.

question: Which part of an SPO serves all customers across the industry verticals?
explanation: The horizontals are general technical services that serve all customers across the verticals.

question: Which part of an SPO holds branch-specific services at application or functional level?
explanation: The industry verticals are branch specific (content specific) services.

question: Infrastructure, testing and BI belong to which part of an SPO?
explanation: The horizontal services are general technical services: infrastructure, testing, BI.

question: An SPO merges with another provider. What happens with its organisational structure?
options: It stays efficient without any change
The old structure always stays the best one for every company
It must be redesigned for the new situation and strategy
Only the logo and the names have to change
explanation: A structure that is very efficient in one situation can be very inefficient in another, for example after a take-over or merger.

question: Which of these is a key pillar of a successful top IT SPO?
options: Specialized, unique services for the customer's business
The lowest price on the market
The widest range of technologies of any provider on the market
explanation: The two key pillars: competent, loyal and motivated employees, and specialized (on the customer's business) unique services.

question: Which of these is NOT a hygiene criterion when selecting an SPO?
explanation: Cultural match is a possible competitive differentiator. The hygiene criteria are financial health, employee stability and the quality of the bench.

question: Which of these is a possible competitive differentiator of an SPO?
options: Financial health and stability of the SPO
explanation: Differentiators: cultural match, superior client facing skills, superior business domain skills, high employee availability.

question: Which employees of an SPO are "on the bench"?
options: Employees who are about to leave the SPO
Employees who already work for the SRO
Employees who are available for new work
Employees who sit on the board
explanation: The best employees are seldom available ("on the bench"), so an SRO must assess the quality of the bench resources.

question: An SPO studies the customer's business, lists its challenges and maps it against its competitors. What is this called?
explanation: Consultative selling: understand the customer's business, assess its market, list its challenges, map it against its competitors, tailor the services.

question: Which of these is NOT a measure against vendor lock-in?
options: Perform at least 20% of the IT services in-house
Let IT staff spread across the IT functions of the SPO
Fill key positions in the outsourced projects yourself
Sign a long contract with a single SPO
explanation: The measures: at least 20% of IT services in-house, IT staff spread across the SPO's functions, key positions filled by the SRO.

question: An SRO performs at least 20% of its IT services in-house. Which risk does this reduce?
options: A high attrition rate at the SPO
A low utilization rate at the SPO
A forced exit of the SPO
explanation: Vendor lock-in is too much dependency on the SPO. Keeping a part in-house avoids it.

question: Which of these is NOT advisable for an SPO?
options: Optimising production in quality and timeliness
Making realistic agreements with the SRO
Saying yes to unrealistic wishes out of fear of losing the business
Rewarding high performing employees financially and with recognition
explanation: DON'T say yes to the SRO's wishes out of fear of losing business if it is not realistic. DO make realistic agreements.

question: An SRO wants to stimulate stable staff at its SPO. Which target is suggested?
explanation: Attrition targets: reward attrition rates below 10%.

question: An SRO demands 10 innovations a year from its SPO. What else should the SRO do?
options: Lower the attrition target of the SPO
Keep the innovation targets secret from the SPO until the year ends
Stop monitoring the SPO to give it room
Facilitate the SPO, for example with a dedicated support team
explanation: It helps to set innovation targets, and to facilitate the SPO in reaching them, for example with a dedicated support team.

question: An SRO pays the SPO per hour of staff and for the materials used. Which contract is this?
explanation: Time and materials: pay staff per hour and for materials.

question: An SRO agrees a set of activities with an SPO for one price. Which contract is this?
explanation: Fixed price: an agreed upon set of activities for a fixed price.

question: An SRO hires professional staff of an SPO to work in its own team. Which contract is this?
explanation: Staff augmentation: hire professional staff.

question: Which statement about the pricing models in a contract is true?
options: Only one pricing model is allowed per contract
Fixed price is the only model that can be used for staff
Time and materials never includes the materials
Variations and combinations of the models can be made
explanation: All kinds of variations and combinations can be made in a contract.

question: Which measure helps an SRO keep knowledge inside when it hires an SPO?
options: Move all the key people to the SPO
Keep SRO personnel on the key positions
Stop documenting the procedures of the outsourced work
Let the SPO hold all the documentation
explanation: Knowledge management: keep SRO personnel on key positions, agree a minimum percentage of SRO personnel, test knowledge retention.

question: A job is light and routine. Which pyramid fits it?
explanation: For light jobs you can apply a lean pyramid, for tough jobs a heavy pyramid.

question: A job is tough and complex. Which pyramid fits it?
options: A heavy pyramid, with more experienced staff
A lean pyramid, with mostly freshers and a few seniors
A flat structure with equal levels
explanation: For tough jobs you need a heavy pyramid (more experience).

question: An SPO team has 3 people with more than 10 years of experience and 30 people with 0 to 3 years. Which pyramid is this?
options: A heavy pyramid, suited for tough jobs
A heavy pyramid, suited for light jobs
A lean pyramid, suited for tough jobs
A lean pyramid, suited for light jobs
explanation: Few experienced people and many freshers: a lean pyramid, which suits light jobs.

question: Which of these can be used to express productivity?
options: The number of meetings that were held per week
The number of incidents or changes handled
The average age of the staff
The size of the office of the SPO
explanation: Productivity is expressed in quantifiable portions: function points, number of incidents, changes, managed applications, managed hardware objects.

question: What is the contract mainly used for?
options: To solve every problem in the daily operation by quoting its rules
To replace the personal contact with the SPO
For operational agreements and as a "big stick" in an escalation
To stop the SPO from innovating
explanation: Contracts set expectations from the start. Day to day, solving problems together matters more than contract rules.

question: Which of these is an advantage of your own overseas IT department?
options: Lower cost than an IT department at headquarters
Higher motivation without any effort from headquarters
No cultural differences to deal with
More focus on IT than on the core business
explanation: For a captive: lower cost, knowledge stays inside, focus on the core business at home.

question: Why do captives often have low motivation?
options: Their employees earn less than the employees at headquarters in the same job
They only take orders from the local government
Their employees dislike working with new technology
They are seen as cost centres and are not recognised by headquarters
explanation: Captives tend to be considered as cost centres and back offices, which gives low empowerment and low motivation. Cultural differences add to this.

question: Which part of exit management decides who owns what was developed during the relationship?
explanation: Intellectual property: determine who owns intellectual property developed during the relationship.

question: In exit management, shadowing for a certain period is an example of...
explanation: Knowledge transition: determine how knowledge must be transferred, for example by shadowing.

question: Which part of exit management covers how and for what the SPO is paid during the exit?
explanation: Financial terms: how and for what is the SPO being paid during the exit procedure.

question: Which part of exit management deals with the documentation the successor needs to take over?
explanation: Deliverables: what documentation is necessary for the successor to take over.

question: Which of these is NOT part of the content of the contract?
options: The private salaries of the SPO's employees
The definition of the services and the personnel profile
explanation: Contract content: price, definition of the services, personnel profile, KPIs, measures against lock-in, requirements, innovation, report content, compensation arrangements, procedures.

question: The SPO misses the agreed availability and has to pay a fine. Which part of the contract is this?
explanation: Compensation arrangements: for example a fine or compensation if requirements are not met.

question: Who should the SRO get to know and align with, especially?
options: The key people of the SPO, especially the horizontals
Only the service managers and the sales team of the SPO
Only the board members of the SPO
Only the sales team of the SPO
explanation: Get to know and align with the SPO's key responsible people (especially the horizontals), not only the service managers.

question: Why should the SRO monitor the SPO?
options: To replace the staff of the SPO by its own staff after a year
To lower the price of the contract
To avoid contact with the employees of the SPO
To prevent the weaknesses of the SPO from becoming apparent
explanation: Utilize the strengths of the SPO and monitor it to prevent its weaknesses becoming apparent.

question: Which of these is NOT a SAFe role?
explanation: SAFe roles: Release Train Engineer, Product Owner (program level), System Architect, Scrum of Scrums Master. The Chief Product Owner is a Scrum@Scale role.

question: How many teams can an Agile Release Train have?
explanation: An ART is a number of teams (5 to 12) working on one product.

question: What is the PI release?
options: The shippable product of each cycle
The plan for the next PI, made by all teams
The list of risks of the ART
explanation: PI release: the shippable product of each cycle. The System Demo reviews the integrated product at the end.

question: Which activity is NOT part of PI Planning Day 1?
options: Final plan review and confidence vote
explanation: The final plan review and confidence vote are on Day 2.

question: When is the Program Board finalized?
options: On PI Planning Day 1, in the morning
On PI Planning Day 2, in the afternoon
During Inspect & Adapt at the end of the PI
At the first sprint review of the PI
explanation: Day 2 afternoon: the Program Board (a visual overview of features and dependencies) is finalized.

question: Which part of PI Planning is for leadership only?
options: The final plan review and confidence vote
explanation: The evening of Day 1: management review and problem solving, attended by the RTE, Product Management, Business Owners and Architects.

question: How often is the PO Sync held in SAFe?
explanation: The PO Sync is a weekly ART-level meeting of POs, Product Management and Business Owners.

question: When does the PI System Demo take place?
options: At the end of every sprint of the team
At the end of the PI (week 10)
explanation: The System Demo is at the end of the PI, with the entire ART and stakeholders.

question: Which team meeting do the team, the PO and the Scrum Master attend at the start of a sprint?
explanation: Sprint Planning: start of the sprint, team + PO + SM.

question: Who attends the Backlog Refinement of a team during the PI?
explanation: Backlog Refinement: ongoing, mid-sprint, team + PO.

question: What is week 0 of the PI table used for?
explanation: Week 0: PI Planning (preparation). Week 1: PI Planning.

question: How many sprints does the execution phase of the PI table contain?
explanation: Execution: weeks 1 to 10, 5 sprints.

question: What is the System Architect responsible for?
options: Facilitating the meetings of the team Scrum Masters
Technical integrity and the architectural guidelines
Prioritising the backlog of the whole program and its risks
explanation: The System Architect ensures technical integrity and defines the architectural guidelines for the teams.

question: Which SAFe role facilitates the meetings of the team Scrum Masters?
explanation: The Scrum of Scrums Master facilitates the team Scrum Master meetings. The RTE facilitates the ART meetings.

question: Which statement about Inspect & Adapt in SAFe is true?
options: It ends with a confidence vote on the actions
Only the Scrum Masters and the RTE take part in it
explanation: Inspect & Adapt: PI System Demo, measurement, problem-solving workshop, and a 15 minute confidence vote on the improvement actions.

question: Which of these belongs to the Executive Action Team in Scrum@Scale?
explanation: The Executive Action Team consists of the CPO, the SoSM, the CEO and company managers.

question: How many teams does one Scrum of Scrums cover in Scrum@Scale?
explanation: A Scrum of Scrums covers 5 teams.

question: How many teams does a Scrum of Scrum of Scrums (SoSoS) cover?
explanation: A SoSoS covers five Scrums of Scrums, so 25 teams.

question: How often does the MetaScrum meet in the table of scaled events?
options: Once per PI, for two days
Only at the end of each sprint
explanation: MetaScrum: weekly (1 hr), CPO + POs + stakeholders.

question: Who attends the Scrum of Scrums in Scrum@Scale?
options: The Chief Product Owner, the Product Owners and the CEO
Only the CEO and the company managers
Scrum Masters, team reps and the Scrum of Scrums Master
explanation: Scrum of Scrums: weekly, 30 to 60 minutes, to resolve delivery impediments.

question: Who attends the MetaScrum?
options: The Scrum Masters, the team representatives and the stakeholders
The Chief Product Owner, the Product Owners and stakeholders
The Scrum of Scrums Master only
All the developers of all teams
explanation: The MetaScrum prioritizes the shared backlog and aligns goals.

question: How long does the Scaled Daily Scrum last?
explanation: Scaled Daily Scrum: daily, 15 minutes, one representative per team plus the SoSM.

question: Which Scrum@Scale event is optional and shows the shared increments at the end of the sprint?
explanation: Scaled Sprint Review: end of the sprint, optional, if cross-team. Multiple teams and stakeholders see the shared increments.

question: In which week of the Scrum@Scale cycle does the preparation take place?
explanation: Week 0: preparation (backlog refinement, vision alignment). Week 1: planning and alignment.

question: Which vote closes the Inspect & Adapt of the Scrum@Scale cycle?
options: A vote of the CEO alone on the budget
A commitment vote on improvements and next priorities
A confidence vote on the PI plan and the program board
explanation: Commitment vote (15 min): confidence in improvements and next priorities, by the full group.

question: Which of these is NOT a Scrum@Scale role?
explanation: S@S roles: Scrum of Scrums Master, Chief Product Owner and the Executive Action Team. The RTE is a SAFe role.

question: Which statement about the Executive MetaScrum is true?
options: It prioritizes the one backlog shared by all teams
It prioritizes a separate backlog for each team and each PO
It facilitates the daily scrums of the teams
It is held only after the sprint reviews
explanation: The Executive MetaScrum (CPO and POs) prioritizes the backlog: one backlog for all teams.

question: Which meeting belongs to the Scrum Masters' cycle in the planning week of Scrum@Scale?
explanation: Week 1: planning and alignment: MetaScrum (PO cycle) and Scrum of Scrums Planning (SM cycle).

question: Which meeting belongs to the Product Owners' cycle in the planning week of Scrum@Scale?
explanation: The MetaScrum is the PO cycle, the Scrum of Scrums Planning the SM cycle.
